nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian random weights $\xi_{ij}$
nodes.statement:
Let $\{\xi_{ij}\}_{i=1,\ldots,N_1\,,j=1,\ldots,N_2}$ a doubly indexed sequence of i.i.d. centred sub-Gaussian r.vs. with 
$$
E[\xi_{ij}\xi_{hk}]=\delta_{ih}\delta_{jk}\,, 
$$
nodes.genus: doubly indexed sequence of i.i.d. centred sub-Gaussian r.vs.

nodes.name: Proportional layer sizes
nodes.statement:
For definiteness we  assume that
$$
\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}\to \alpha\in(0,1)\,.
$$

nodes.name: Random matrix $\Xi$ and sample covariance matrix
nodes.statement: We shall look at this sequence in two different ways, namely as entries of a $N_1\times N_2$ random matrix $\Xi$ or a collection of $N_2$ patterns in $\mathbb{R}^{N_1}$, defining a sample covariance matrix  $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1\times N_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: View the weights as an $N_1\times N_2$ matrix $\Xi$ or as $N_2$ patterns with sample covariance $\Xi\Xi^T/N_2$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue and singular value notation
nodes.statement: For $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ we denote its eigenvalues as $\lambda_i:=\lambda_{i}(A)$, $i=1,\ldots N$; for $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1\times N_2}$ we denote its singular values as $\sigma_i:=\sigma_{i}(A)$, $i=1,\ldots N_1$.

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur law (P1)
nodes.statement:
The empirical distribution of the eigenvalues of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law:
$$
\frac{1}{N_1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_1}\delta(\lambda-\lambda_i(\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T)) \rightharpoonup \rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\quad \mathbb P-a.s.
$$
where
\begin{equation} \rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha):= (2-\frac{1}{\alpha})^+\delta_0(\lambda) +\frac{(1-\alpha)}{2\pi \alpha}\frac{\sqrt{(\lambda-\lambda_-)(\lambda_+-\lambda)}}{\lambda}1_{[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]}(\lambda)
\end{equation}
with  $\lambda_{\pm}:=\left(1\pm\sqrt{\alpha/(1-\alpha)}\right)^2$.
conclusions: The empirical distribution of the eigenvalues of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law
nodes.statement_short: The eigenvalue empirical distribution of $\Xi\Xi^T/N_2$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law $\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)$.

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur density $\rho_{MP}$
nodes.statement: \rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha):= (2-\frac{1}{\alpha})^+\delta_0(\lambda) +\frac{(1-\alpha)}{2\pi \alpha}\frac{\sqrt{(\lambda-\lambda_-)(\lambda_+-\lambda)}}{\lambda}1_{[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]}(\lambda)
nodes.label: eq:MP

nodes.name: Spectral localisation of the sample covariance (P2)
conclusions: The spectrum of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ is localised in an interval with large probability
nodes.statement_short: Operator-norm deviation of $\Xi\Xi^T/N_2$ from the identity beyond $\sqrt{\lambda_+}-1+t$ has probability $\le 2e^{-N_1t^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian operator norm tail bound
nodes.statement: \mathbb P(\|\frac {1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T-\mathbb I\|_{op}\geq t+\sqrt{\lambda_+}-1)\leq 2e^{-\frac {N_1t^2}{2}}\,.
nodes.label: eq:impo-spectrum

nodes.name: Hopfield models and restricted Boltzmann machines
nodes.statement: We will deal with two kind of Boltzmann machines: Hopfield models (HMs) and restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs).

nodes.name: Hamiltonians of HM and RBM
nodes.statement_short: HM energy is minus the normalised pattern-overlap quadratic form; RBM energy is the bilinear coupling $-\sum\xi_{ij}x_iy_j/\sqrt{N_1+N_2}$.

nodes.name: Sphere $S^N(R)$
nodes.statement: Let $S^{N}(R)$ be the $(N-1)$-dimensional sphere in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with radius $R\sqrt N$.

nodes.name: Spherical and Gaussian priors
Spherical and Gaussian prior measures
nodes.statement: \begin{cases} \sigma_{N,R}(dx)&\mbox{uniform on $S^N(R)$}\,;\\ \gamma_{N,\theta}(dx)&\mbox{centred Gaussian with covariance $\theta \mathbb I$}\,. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:prior

nodes.name: Regularising function $r$
nodes.statement:
Let  $r\,:\mathbb{R}\mapsto\mathbb{R}$ such that there is $\varepsilon>0$ with
$$
\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{r(x)}{x^{2+\varepsilon}}=\infty\,.
$$

nodes.name: Regularised (sub-Gaussian) prior $\rho_N$
Regularised prior density
nodes.statement: \rho_N(dx):= e^{-Nr\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}\right)}\gamma_{N,\theta}(dx)\,.
nodes.label: eq:Reg-prior1

nodes.name: Two-layer regularising function $r(x,y)$
nodes.statement:
We introduce some $r\,:\,\mathbb{R}^2\mapsto \mathbb{R}$ so that
$$
\lim_{x^2+y^2\to\infty} \frac{r(x,y)}{x^2}=\lim_{x^2+y^2\to\infty} \frac{r(x,y)}{y^2}=\infty\,.
$$

nodes.name: Two-layer regularised prior $\rho^2$
Two-layer regularised prior density
nodes.statement: \rho^2_{N_1,N_2}(dxdy):= e^{-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1},\frac{\|y\|}{\sqrt N_2}\right)}\gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx)\gamma_{N_2,\theta}(dy)\,.
nodes.label: eq:Reg-prior2

nodes.name: Low rank matrix factorisation regulariser
nodes.statement: A simple example is low rank matrix factorisation with Gaussian priors in which $r(x,y)=x^2y^2/2$ \cite{leo}.

nodes.name: Spherical shells
Spherical shell set
nodes.statement: S_{N,R,\varepsilon}:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N\,:\,R-\varepsilon\leq\|x\|_2\leq R+\varepsilon\}\,.
nodes.label: eq:Sfshell

nodes.name: Uniform probability on a shell
nodes.statement:
We denote (here and further $|A|$ is the Lebesgue measure of the set $A$)
$$
\sigma_{N,R.\varepsilon}(dx):=|S_{\varepsilon,N,R}|^{-1}1_{\{S_{\varepsilon,N,R}\}}(x)dx\,
$$
the uniform probability on a shell and note that it is a.c. w.r.t. $\gamma_{N,\theta}$.

nodes.name: Shell volume expansion
nodes.statement: |S_{\varepsilon,N,R}|=\varepsilon|S_{N,R}|+\OOO{\varepsilon^2}\,.
nodes.label: eq:shells-surface

nodes.name: Generic priors $\mu$, $\mu^2$
nodes.statement: Let $\mu_{(\cdot)}\in\{\sigma_{(\cdot)},\gamma_{(\cdot)},\rho_{(\cdot)}\}$ and $\mu^2_{(\cdot)}\in\{\sigma_{(\cdot)},\gamma_{(\cdot)}\}\otimes \{\sigma_{(\cdot)},\gamma_{(\cdot)}\}\cup\{\rho_{(\cdot)}^2\}$ denote one prior among the one introduced before respectively for the one-layer and the bipartite machine.

nodes.name: Gibbs measures of HM and RBM
Partition function
nodes.statement: The normalisation $Z_{N_1,N_2,\beta}$ is called partition function and it needs not to be the same, despite the symbol.

nodes.name: Free energy
Free energies of HM and RBM
nodes.statement: A^{HM}_{N_1,N_2}(\beta):=\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\qquad A^{RBM}_{N_1,N_2}(\beta):=\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\,.
nodes.label: eq:free

nodes.name: Thermodynamic limit
nodes.statement:
Most interesting is to evaluate the last quantities in the so-called thermodynamic limit, namely
$$
N_1,N_2\to\infty\,,\quad\mbox{such that }\qquad \lim_{N_1,N_2}\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}=:\alpha>0\,.
$$

nodes.name: High-load regime
nodes.statement: The regime $\alpha\neq0,1$ is called high-load and we will stick to that in this work.

nodes.name: Self-averaging of the free energy
nodes.statement: Being Lipschitz functions of the weights, free energies always satisfies a concentration inequality which ensures their a.s. convergence to the expected value. This self-averaging property will be exploited throughout without further mention.

nodes.name: Equal parameters on both layers
nodes.statement: For simplicity we will assume always the distributions of the two layers to have the same parameters, \textit{i.e. } radius and variance.

nodes.name: Free energy notation $A_\mu(X,\alpha,\beta)$
nodes.statement: In general $A_\mu(X,\alpha,\beta)$ denotes the free energy of a BM with prior $\mu$ whose parameters are $X$.

nodes.name: Hat notation for spherical shell priors
nodes.statement: Only exception, the quantities of interest referred to spherical shell priors are indicated by $\widehat \cdot$ for all the models.

nodes.name: Marginalisation of the Gaussian layer
nodes.statement:
Marginalisation is the usual trick of RBMs. The two layers are coupled linearly, so that one can integrate out \'a la Stratonovich the units from the Gaussian layer in the partition function of a RBM to obtain the partition function of a HM (with $\beta^2$ replacing $\beta$). 
All the relevant quantities (e.g. Gibbs measures, free energy, order parameters etc) of one model can be computed directly from the one of the other one. For instance the equivalence $HM_\sigma\leftrightarrow RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$ at the level of Gibbs measure reads as
$$
Z^{-1}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\sigma_{N_2,R}(dx)\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_2}}\gamma_{N_2,\theta}(dy)e^{\beta H_{N_1,N_2}^{RBM}}=Z^{-1}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\sigma_{N_1,R}(dx)e^{\frac{\beta^2}{\theta^2} H^{HM}_{N_1}}\,,
$$
since the  partition functions of the two models are numerically the same.
nodes.section: Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: Integrating out a Gaussian layer of an RBM (Hubbard-Stratonovich) gives the HM partition function with $\beta^2$ in place of $\beta$.

nodes.name: Heuristic sketch of $RBM_{\sigma\sigma}\leftrightarrow RBM_{\rho^2}$
nodes.section: Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: Disintegrate the Gaussian prior into spheres, express the inner integral via the spherical free energy, and evaluate by Laplace's method.

nodes.name: Legendre equivalences of spherical and Gaussian Boltzmann machines
nodes.statement: Assume $\bf P1), P2)$ and let $\rho_N, \rho^2_N$ be defined as in (\ref{eq:Reg-prior1}), (\ref{eq:Reg-prior2}) and discussion around. Then \begin{itemize} \item[i)] $HM_{\sigma}\xleftrightarrow{LT} HM_{\rho}$: \begin{equation} A_\rho(\theta,\alpha,\beta)=\alpha \sup_{R>0}\left( \alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma}(R,\beta) -\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\log R- r(R) -\frac12(\log\theta-1) \right)\,; \end{equation} \begin{equation} A_{\sigma}(R,\beta)=\alpha \inf_{\theta>0}\left(\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\alpha^{-1}A_\rho(\theta,\alpha,\beta) -\log R+ r(R)+\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,. \end{equation} \item[ii)] $RBM_{\sigma\sigma}\xleftrightarrow{LT} RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$: \begin{equation} A_{\sigma,\gamma}(\theta,R_2,\alpha,\beta)=\alpha\sup_{R_1>0}\left(\alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma\sigma}(R_1,R_2,\beta)-\frac{R_1^2}{2\theta}+\log R_1 -\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,; \end{equation} \begin{equation} A_{\sigma\sigma}(R_1,R_2,\beta)=\alpha\inf_{\theta>0}\left(\frac{R_1^2}{2\theta}+\alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma,\gamma}(\theta,R_2,\alpha,\beta)-\log R_1+\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,. \end{equation} \item[iii)] $RBM_{\sigma\sigma}\xleftrightarrow{LT} RBM_{\rho^2}$: \begin{equation} A_{\rho^2}(\theta,\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{R_1,R_2>0}\left(A_{\sigma\sigma}(R_1,R_2)-\frac{\alpha R_1^2+(1-\alpha)R_2^2}{2\theta}+\log(R_1^\alpha R_2^{1-\alpha})-\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)}r(R_1,R_2)-\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,; \end{equation} \begin{equation} A(R_1,R_2)=\inf_{\theta_1,\theta_2>0}\left(\frac{\alpha R_1^2}{2\theta_1}+\frac{(1-\alpha)R_2^2}{2\theta_2}+A_{\rho^2}(\theta_1,\theta_2,\alpha,\beta)-\log(R_1^\alpha R_2^{1-\alpha})+\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)}r(R_1,R_2)+\frac12(\log\theta_1^\alpha\theta_2^{1-\alpha}-1)\right)\,. \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.section: Main result and organisation of the paper
assumptions: $\rho_N, \rho^2_N$ be defined as in (\ref{eq:Reg-prior1}), (\ref{eq:Reg-prior2}) and discussion around
conclusions: $HM_{\sigma}\xleftrightarrow{LT} HM_{\rho}$: \begin{equation} A_\rho(\theta,\alpha,\beta)=\alpha \sup_{R>0}\left( \alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma}(R,\beta) -\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\log R- r(R) -\frac12(\log\theta-1) \right)\,; \end{equation} \begin{equation} A_{\sigma}(R,\beta)=\alpha \inf_{\theta>0}\left(\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\alpha^{-1}A_\rho(\theta,\alpha,\beta) -\log R+ r(R)+\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Free energies of spherical and (regularised) Gaussian HMs and RBMs are related by Legendre transforms in the radius / inverse variance.

nodes.name: Convex minimisation principle for doubly spherical RBM
nodes.statement: In any case it is remarkable that the free energy of a doubly spherical RBM satisfies a fully convex minimisation principle, which is a crucial difference compared to the $\min\max$ of Gauss-Bernoulli \cite{bgg} and Bernoulli-Bernoulli RBMs \cite{Bip}.

nodes.name: Free energy of the spherical Hopfield model
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\sigma}$. It holds $P$-a.s. \begin{equation} \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} = \alpha\min_{2q\geq \beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(q R^2 -\frac 12\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right)\,. \end{equation}
conclusions: It holds $P$-a.s. \begin{equation} \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} = \alpha\min_{2q\geq \beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(q R^2 -\frac 12\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The spherical Hopfield free energy converges a.s. to a convex variational formula in $q$ over the Marchenko-Pastur law.
nodes.label: Th:HM-sfer

nodes.name: Variational formula for spherical HM free energy
nodes.statement: \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} = \alpha\min_{2q\geq \beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(q R^2 -\frac 12\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right)\,.
nodes.label: eq:AHMsfer

nodes.name: Free energy of the doubly spherical RBM
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $RBM_{\sigma\sigma}$ and $\alpha\leq \frac 12$. It holds $P$-a.s. \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} &=&\min_{ab\geq \beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(\frac{R^2}{2}\left(\alpha a + (1-\alpha) b\right) -\frac 1 2 (1-2\alpha)\log(b)\right. \nonumber \\ &-&\left.\frac \alpha2\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right) \,. \end{eqnarray}
conclusions: It holds $P$-a.s. \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} &=&\min_{ab\geq \beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(\frac{R^2}{2}\left(\alpha a + (1-\alpha) b\right) -\frac 1 2 (1-2\alpha)\log(b)\right. \nonumber \\ &-&\left.\frac \alpha2\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right) \,. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The doubly spherical RBM free energy converges a.s. to a convex minimum over Lagrange multipliers $a,b$ with $ab\ge\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$.
nodes.label: Th:Bip-sfer

nodes.name: Variational formula for spherical RBM free energy
nodes.statement: \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} &=&\min_{ab\geq \beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(\frac{R^2}{2}\left(\alpha a + (1-\alpha) b\right) -\frac 1 2 (1-2\alpha)\log(b)\right. \nonumber \\ &-&\left.\frac \alpha2\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right) \,.

nodes.name: Convenience of $\alpha\le 1/2$
nodes.statement: The choice $\alpha\leq\frac12$ is just a matter of convenience as it will be clear that pre-choosing the largest layer simplifies a lot the notations. For $\alpha\geq \frac12$ one should bear in mind that the Marchenko-Pastur distribution (\ref{eq:MP}) has an atom in zero.

nodes.name: Spherical shells approximate the spherical prior
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\sigma_\varepsilon}$, $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma}$ or $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma_\varepsilon}$. Then it is $$ \lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\lim_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}=\lim_{N_1,N_2}\lim_{\varepsilon\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\,. $$
assumptions: $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\sigma_\varepsilon}$, $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma}$ or $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma_\varepsilon}$
nodes.statement_short: The limits $\varepsilon\to0$ and $N\to\infty$ of the shell-prior free energy commute.
nodes.label: lemma-gusci

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: In this proof we write $N$ to mean $N_1$ or $N_2$ and by $A^{\sigma}(R; \beta)$ the free energy of a spherical model of radius $R$, according to the context. No further details are needed. By Fubini and the mean value theorem there is a $R^*_\varepsilon\in[R\sqrt N-\varepsilon,R\sqrt N+\varepsilon]$ for which $$ \widehat A_{N_1,N_2}=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)\,. $$ By a simple change of variables we have $$ A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R; c_{N,\varepsilon}\beta)\,, $$ with $c_{N,\varepsilon}:=R^2_\varepsilon/R^2N$. Therefore by Lipschitz continuity of the free energy w.r.t. $\beta$ $$ |A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}-\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}|\leq \frac\varepsilon N\,. $$ This, combined with $A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$, gives the assert.
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem places the shell at a sphere radius; rescaling into $\beta$ and Lipschitz continuity in $\beta$ give an $\varepsilon/N$ error.

nodes.name: Notation
nodes.statement: In this proof we write $N$ to mean $N_1$ or $N_2$ and by $A^{\sigma}(R; \beta)$ the free energy of a spherical model of radius $R$, according to the context. No further details are needed.
nodes.statement_short: Fix notation

nodes.name: Mean value theorem
nodes.statement:
By Fubini and the mean value theorem there is a $R^*_\varepsilon\in[R\sqrt N-\varepsilon,R\sqrt N+\varepsilon]$ for which
$$
\widehat A_{N_1,N_2}=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem picks a radius in the shell

nodes.name: Change of variables
nodes.statement:
By a simple change of variables we have
$$
A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R; c_{N,\varepsilon}\beta)\,, 
$$
with $c_{N,\varepsilon}:=R^2_\varepsilon/R^2N$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale radius into inverse temperature

nodes.name: Lipschitz bound
nodes.statement:
Therefore by Lipschitz continuity of the free energy w.r.t. $\beta$
$$
|A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}-\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}|\leq \frac\varepsilon N\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz bound in $\beta$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: This, combined with $A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$, gives the assert.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude commutation of limits

nodes.name: Diagonalisation of the Hopfield energy
nodes.statement:
The best advantage of the spherical prior is that one can diagonalise the energy (\ref{eq:HM}):
$$
H(x)=-(1-\alpha)\sum_{i=1}^{N_1}\lambda_ix_i^2\,.
$$

nodes.label: lemma:HM-sfer

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement_short: Lagrange-multiplier upper bound via Gaussian integral, then reverse bound by controlling shell complements. The key step picks $q$ at the unique minimiser of the convex trial function $\tilde A$.

nodes.name: Representation of the shell partition function (HM)
nodes.statement: \varepsilon \hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\beta,\alpha,R)&=& \varepsilon\ e^{q R^2 N_1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}}\sigma_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}(dz)e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}\\ &\leq&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)z_i^2/2}\nonumber\\ &=&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N}}|}e^{-\frac 12\sum_i^N\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)}\nonumber\,,
nodes.label: eq:reprZ-Hop

nodes.name: Lower bound by max of three trial functions
nodes.statement: \lim\inf_{N_1,N_2}\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\tilde\varepsilon}\geq\max\left(\tilde A(q), A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q), A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)\right),
nodes.label: eq:max( , , )

nodes.name: Trial function $A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}$
nodes.statement: A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)&=&\alpha(q+\eta)R^2-\alpha\tilde\varepsilon\eta-\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2(q+\eta)-\beta\lambda)-\alpha\log R-\frac\alpha2;

nodes.name: Trial function $A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}$
nodes.statement: A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)&=&\alpha(q-\eta)R^2-\alpha\tilde\varepsilon\eta-\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2(q-\eta)-\beta\lambda)-\alpha\log R-\frac\alpha2.

nodes.name: Difference $\Delta_-$
nodes.statement: \Delta_-(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)= -\alpha\eta(R^2-\tilde\varepsilon)+\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log\left(\frac{2(q+\eta)-\beta\lambda}{2q-\beta\lambda}\right);

nodes.name: Difference $\Delta_+$
nodes.statement: \Delta_+(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)= \alpha\eta(R^2+\tilde\varepsilon)+\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log\left(\frac{2(q-\eta)-\beta\lambda}{2q-\beta\lambda}\right)\,.

nodes.name: Derivative condition for $\Delta_-$
nodes.statement: 0<-(R^2-\tilde\varepsilon)+\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{2q-\beta\lambda}=\tilde \varepsilon-\partial_q \tilde A(q)\,.
nodes.label: eq:upper-bound-epsi1

nodes.name: Derivative condition for $\Delta_+$
nodes.statement: 0\leq(R^2+\tilde\varepsilon)+\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{2q-\beta\lambda}=\tilde \varepsilon+\partial_q \tilde A(q).
nodes.label: eq:upper-bound-epsi2

nodes.name: Lower bound by minimum of $\tilde A$
nodes.statement: \lim\inf_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2.\tilde \varepsilon}\geq \min_{q\geq\beta\lambda_+}\tilde A(q) \,.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement:
Let $2q>\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$. Then using (\ref{eq:shells-surface}) we have 
\begin{eqnarray}
\varepsilon \hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\beta,\alpha,R)&=& \varepsilon\ e^{q R^2 N_1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}}\sigma_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}(dz)e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2} \\
&\leq&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)z_i^2/2}\nonumber\\
&=&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N}}|}e^{-\frac 12\sum_i^N\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)}\nonumber\,,
\end{eqnarray}
therefore, since $\frac 1{N_1} \log \left(|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}| /\sqrt{2\pi}^{N_1}  \right) \to \log R +\frac 1 2$ and thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac1{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\beta,\alpha,R)\leq \alpha q R^2 -\frac \alpha2\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda)-\alpha\log R-\frac\alpha2=:\tilde A(q)\,,
$$
whence, as $\tilde A(q)$ is continuous, 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\beta,\alpha,R)\leq\min_{2q\geq\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\tilde A(q).
$$
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound via Gaussian integral for any admissible $q$

nodes.name: Convexity
nodes.statement:
Moreover for $2q>\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$
$$
\partial_q^2 \tilde A(q)=2\alpha\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda)^2}>0,
$$
thus $\tilde A(q)$ is  convex and the minimum is attained in a unique point $\bar q$.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\tilde A$ gives a unique minimiser

nodes.name: Reverse bound setup
nodes.statement:
Now the reverse bound. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $S^c_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}$ the complementary set of the shell $S_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}$. It holds
$$
\varepsilon \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}=e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}-e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac N2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{S_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}^c}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Split shell partition function into whole space minus complement

nodes.name: Complement bound
nodes.statement_short: Bound the shell-complement integral

nodes.name: Max lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound by max of three trial functions

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement:
Now we show that if $\bar q$ is the unique minimiser of $\tilde A(q)$ it is for $\eta$ small enough
$$
\tilde A(\bar q)=\max\left(\tilde A(\bar q), A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; \bar q), A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; \bar q)\right)\,,
$$
which will conclude the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing $\tilde A(\bar q)$ dominates

nodes.statement_short: Define differences $\Delta_\pm$

nodes.name: Condition for $\Delta_-$
nodes.statement_short: Concavity gives derivative condition for $\Delta_-$

nodes.name: Condition for $\Delta_+$
nodes.statement_short: Convexity gives derivative condition for $\Delta_+$

nodes.name: Stationary point
nodes.statement:
Combining (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi1}) and (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi2}) we get
$$
-\tilde\varepsilon\leq \left.\partial_q \tilde A(q)\right|_{q=\tilde q}<\tilde\varepsilon\,,,
$$
that is $\tilde q$ is the unique stationary point of $\tilde A(q)$.
nodes.statement_short: Conditions force the stationary point

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement_short: Matching lower bound; let $\tilde\varepsilon\to0$

nodes.name: Singular value decomposition of the RBM energy
nodes.statement:
First step is to use the singular value decomposition of the matrix $\{\xi_{ij}\}$ to write
\begin{equation} \frac{1}{\sqrt{N_1+N_2}}(x,\xi y)=\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i\,,
\end{equation}
where $\tilde x,\tilde y$ are related respectively to $x,y$ by an orthogonal transformation.

nodes.name: Diagonalised RBM energy
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{\sqrt{N_1+N_2}}(x,\xi y)=\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i\,,
nodes.label: eq:diagRBM

nodes.name: Negligibility of large singular values for spherical RBM
nodes.statement: There exists $c,C>0$ so that $$E[A_{N_1,N_2}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>\bar\sigma\}}]\leq Ce^{-cN_1}\,,$$ where $\bar \sigma:= 1+\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}}$.
conclusions: There exists $c,C>0$ so that $$E[A_{N_1,N_2}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>\bar\sigma\}}]\leq Ce^{-cN_1}\,,$$ where $\bar \sigma:= 1+\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.5
nodes.statement: For any $a>\bar\sigma$ we compute $$ E[e^{\alpha\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]=E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\leq a\}}]+E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>a\}}]\,. $$ The first summand is easily estimated by \begin{equation} E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\leq a\}}]\leq E[e^{\beta a\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]\leq E[e^{\beta a \|\tilde x\|\|\tilde y\|}]\,. \end{equation} Arguing as in the proof of \cite[Proposition 1]{legendre} we can write for a $C>0$ \begin{equation} E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>a\}}]\leq Ca\sqrt{2\pi (N_1+N_2)}e^{\frac{\beta^2}{2(N_1+N_2)}\|\tilde x\|^2\|\tilde y\|^2}\,. \end{equation} Then (\ref{eq:bound1}) and (\ref{eq:bound2}) give an annealed bound for the free energy: \begin{equation} \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_N\leq \max\left(\bar\sigma\beta\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)}R^2\,,\,\,\frac12 \beta^2\alpha(1-\alpha)R^2_1R^2_2 \right)<\infty\,. \end{equation} With this bound at hand, we repeat mutatis mutandis the steps of the proof of \cite[Lemma 1]{legendre} to get \begin{equation} E[A_{N_1,N_2}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>\bar\sigma\}}]\leq\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)\beta^2R^4+a^2}\sqrt{P(\|\Xi\Xi^T/N_2-\mathbb I\|_{op}\geq t+\sqrt{\lambda_+}-1)} \end{equation} and the assert follows from (\ref{eq:impo-spectrum}).
nodes.statement_short: Split by largest singular value, bound each part annealedly, then repeat the earlier lemma's argument with the spectral tail bound.

nodes.name: Bound on typical-spectrum contribution
nodes.statement: E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\leq a\}}]\leq E[e^{\beta a\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]\leq E[e^{\beta a \|\tilde x\|\|\tilde y\|}]\,.
nodes.label: eq:bound1

nodes.name: Bound on atypical-spectrum contribution
nodes.statement: E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>a\}}]\leq Ca\sqrt{2\pi (N_1+N_2)}e^{\frac{\beta^2}{2(N_1+N_2)}\|\tilde x\|^2\|\tilde y\|^2}\,.
nodes.label: eq:bound2

nodes.name: Annealed bound on RBM free energy
nodes.statement: \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_N\leq \max\left(\bar\sigma\beta\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)}R^2\,,\,\,\frac12 \beta^2\alpha(1-\alpha)R^2_1R^2_2 \right)<\infty\,.

nodes.name: Bound on large-singular-value contribution
nodes.statement: E[A_{N_1,N_2}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>\bar\sigma\}}]\leq\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)\beta^2R^4+a^2}\sqrt{P(\|\Xi\Xi^T/N_2-\mathbb I\|_{op}\geq t+\sqrt{\lambda_+}-1)}

For any $a>\bar\sigma$ we compute
$$
E[e^{\alpha\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]=E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\leq a\}}]+E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>a\}}]\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Split expectation by largest singular value

We split $S_{1,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\setminus S^c_{1,\varepsilon}$ and $S_{2,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\setminus S^c_{2,\varepsilon}$ and set $S_{\varepsilon}:=S_{1,\varepsilon}	imes S_{2,\varepsilon}$. onumber\ S_\varepsilon^{\kappa,2}&:=&\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,, y\in\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\,:\,\, \kappa(\|y\|^2-R^2N_2)\geq \varepsilon N_2\,\}\,.
onumber \end{eqnarray} Thus $S_\varepsilon^c= igcup_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}}S_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}$. Moreover we pick $\eta>0$ small enough and set  egin{eqnarray} M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) &:=& \left( { egin{array}{cc} a+(2-j)\kappa\eta & - eta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i \ - eta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i & b+(j-1)\kappa\eta \ \end{array} } ight)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]
onumber\ M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta)&:=&\mathrm{diag}(0,b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,.
onumber \end{eqnarray} Also, we put  egin{eqnarray} Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}&:=& \exp\left( rac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)+ rac{(2-j)N_1\kappa\eta a}{2}+ rac{(j-1)N_2\kappa\eta b}{2}-\eta \varepsilon N_jight)
onumber\ &&\int_{S_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}}  rac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( - rac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) z_i)ight)
onumber\ \end{eqnarray} so that $$ (ef{eq:II-termRBM})=-\sum_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j=1,2} Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}\,. $$ We conclude that for any $\eta>0$ sufficiently small and $a,b$ with $ab>(1-\alpha) eta^2\lambda_+$  egin{equation} \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\geq \max( ar A(a,b), \{A_\varepsilon^{\kappa, j}(\eta; a,b)\}_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}})\,, \end{equation} where  egin{eqnarray} A_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)&:=&-\eta\varepsilon+ rac12\alpha a(R^2+(2-j)\kappa\eta)+ rac12(1-\alpha) b(R^2+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
onumber\ &-&\log R - rac12- rac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log (b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
onumber\ &-& rac\alpha2 \int ho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log((a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\alpha) eta^2\lambda)\,. 
onumber \end{eqnarray} In analogy with the proof of Theorem ef{Th:HM-sfer} we define  egin{eqnarray} \Delta_{\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)&:=& ar A(a,b)-A_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)
onumber\ &=&\eta \varepsilon-(2-j)\kappa rac{\eta\alpha a}{2}-(j-1)\kappa rac{\eta(1-\alpha) b}{2}+ rac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
onumber\ &+& rac\alpha2 \int ho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log\left( rac{(a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\alpha) eta^2\lambda}{ab-(1-\alpha) eta^2\lambda}ight)\,.
onumber \end{eqnarray} We need to show that $\Delta_{\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)\geq0$ for $\eta>0$ small. As before, to do so it suffices to prove the derivative in the origin to be non-negative uniformly in $\varepsilon>0$. Bearing in mind (ef{eq:grad1RBM}), (ef{eq:grad2RBM}) we have  egin{eqnarray}  rac{d}{d\eta} \Delta_{\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}(\eta) ig|_{\eta=0}&=&\varepsilon+(2-j)\kappa\left(- rac{a\alpha R^2}{2}+ rac\alpha2 \int ho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\left( rac{b}{ab-(1-\alpha) eta^2\lambda}ight)ight)
onumber\ &+&(j-1)\kappa\left(- rac{b(1-\alpha) R^2}{2}+ rac{1-2\alpha}{2b}+ rac\alpha2 \int ho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\left( rac{a}{ab-(1-\alpha) eta^2\lambda}ight)ight)
onumber\ &=&\varepsilon-(2-j)\kappa\partial_a ar A-(j-1)\kappa\partial_b ar A\geq0\,. 
onumber \end{eqnarray} Since the inequality must hold for any $\varepsilon>0$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$, we have to pick $( ar a,  ar b)=\arg\min  ar A$. Therefore $$ \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\geq \max( ar A( ar a, ar b), \{A^{\varepsilon,\kappa_1,\kappa_2}(\eta;  ar a, ar b)\}_{\kappa_1,\kappa_2\in\{-1,1\}})= \min_{ab> eta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+} ar A( a, b)\quad  orall \varepsilon>0\,, $$ which combined with (ef{eq:upperbound.RBM}) proves the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Lagrange multipliers $a,b$ reduce to $2\times2$ Gaussian blocks for an upper bound; the reverse bound controls four shell complements. The key step picks $(a,b)$ at the minimiser of the convex $\bar A$.

nodes.name: Representation of the RBM partition function
nodes.statement: Z_{N_1,N_2}&=&\int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy) \exp\left( \sqrt{1-\alpha} \beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}x_iy_i\sigma_i-\frac a2 \|x\|^2-\frac b2 \|y\|^2+\frac a2 R^2N_1+\frac b2 R^2N_2\right)\nonumber\\ &=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy)\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\,,
nodes.label: eq:repr-Z-RBM

nodes.name: Upper bound on shell RBM partition function
nodes.statement: \varepsilon^2\hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}&\leq& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \frac{(2\pi)^{\frac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{\frac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} \int \frac{dx dy}{\sqrt{2\pi}^N}\exp\left( -\frac 12\sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right),\nonumber\\ &=& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \frac{(2\pi)^{\frac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{\frac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} b^{-\frac{N_2-N_1}{2}} \prod_{i=1}^{N_1}(ab-\beta^2(1-\alpha)\sigma^2_i)^{-\frac 12}\,.

nodes.name: Trial function $\bar A(a,b)$
nodes.statement: \bar A(a,b):= \frac {R^2}{2} (a\alpha+b(1-\alpha))-\log R-\frac12-\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log b -\frac{\alpha}{2}\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda)\,.
nodes.label: eq:RBM-trial

nodes.name: Upper bound by minimum of $\bar A$
nodes.statement: \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \min_{ab>(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda_+} \bar A(a,b)\,.
nodes.label: eq:upperbound.RBM

nodes.name: Gradient of $\bar A$ in $a$
nodes.statement: \partial_a \bar A(a,b)&=&\frac{\alpha R^2}{2}-\frac\alpha2\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\frac{b}{ab- (1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}\,;
nodes.label: eq:grad1RBM

nodes.name: Gradient of $\bar A$ in $b$
nodes.statement: \partial_b \bar A(a,b)&=&\frac{(1-\alpha)R^2}{2} -\frac{1-2\alpha}{2b}-\frac\alpha2\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\frac{a}{ab- (1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}\,.
nodes.label: eq:grad2RBM

nodes.name: Shell RBM partition function decomposition
nodes.statement: \varepsilon^2 \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}&:=&\varepsilon^2\int\sigma_{N_1, R,\varepsilon}(dx)\sigma_{N_2,R,\varepsilon}(dy)e^{-\beta H_N(x,y)}\nonumber\\ &=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\times \mathbb{R}^{N_2}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\nonumber\\ &-&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{S^c_{\varepsilon}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\,,
nodes.label: eq:II-termRBM

nodes.name: Lower bound by max of trial functions (RBM)
nodes.statement: \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\geq \max(\bar A(a,b), \{A_\varepsilon^{\kappa, j}(\eta; a,b)\}_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}})\,,

nodes.name: Block representation
nodes.statement:
Now  start from (\ref{eq:diagRBM}) and write for any $a,b$ such that $ab>\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$
\begin{eqnarray}
Z_{N_1,N_2}&=&\int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy) \exp\left( \sqrt{1-\alpha} \beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}x_iy_i\sigma_i-\frac a2 \|x\|^2-\frac b2 \|y\|^2+\frac a2 R^2N_1+\frac b2 R^2N_2\right)\nonumber\\
&=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy)\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right) \,,
\end{eqnarray}
where we have defined 
$$
z^T_i := \begin{cases}
(x_i,y_i)&i=1,\ldots , N_1\,,\\
(0,y_i)&i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2
\end{cases}$$
and the $2\times 2$ symmetric positively defined matrix 
$$
M_i :=
  \left( {\begin{array}{cc}
   a & -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i \\
   -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i & b \\
\end{array} } \right)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]\qquad M_i:=\mathrm{diag}(0,b)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite partition function with Lagrange multipliers in $2\times2$ blocks

nodes.name: Gaussian bound
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian integral upper bound

nodes.name: Trial function
nodes.statement:
We introduce
\begin{equation} \bar A(a,b):= \frac {R^2}{2} (a\alpha+b(1-\alpha))-\log R-\frac12-\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log b -\frac{\alpha}{2}\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda)\,.
\end{equation}
and 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \bar A(a,b)\,,\quad \forall a,b>0\,:\,\,ab>(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda_+\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Define trial function $\bar A(a,b)$ bounding the free energy

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement_short: Convexity gives upper bound by minimum

nodes.name: Gradient
nodes.statement_short: Record gradient of $\bar A$

nodes.name: Reverse bound setup
nodes.statement:
For the reverse bound consider again  spherical shells around $S_{R,N_1}$ and $S_{R,N_2}$ of thickness $\varepsilon$, that we name respectively $S_{1,\varepsilon}$ and $S_{2,\varepsilon}$. We split $S_{1,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\setminus S^c_{1,\varepsilon}$ and $S_{2,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\setminus S^c_{2,\varepsilon}$ and set $S_{\varepsilon}:=S_{1,\varepsilon}\times S_{2,\varepsilon}$. We have

\begin{eqnarray}
\varepsilon^2 \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}&:=&\varepsilon^2\int\sigma_{N_1, R,\varepsilon}(dx)\sigma_{N_2,R,\varepsilon}(dy)e^{-\beta H_N(x,y)}\nonumber\\
&=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\times \mathbb{R}^{N_2}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\nonumber\\
&-&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{S^c_{\varepsilon}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right) \,,
\end{eqnarray}
where we used again the representation (\ref{eq:repr-Z-RBM}).
nodes.statement_short: Split shell partition function

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: The free energy associated to the first summand was already computed above in the thermodynamic limit. Therefore we have to upper bound the second summand.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounding complement term

nodes.name: Four pieces
nodes.statement_short: Decompose complement into four pieces with shifted multipliers

nodes.name: Max lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound by max of trial functions

nodes.name: Differences
nodes.statement_short: Define differences $\Delta^{\kappa,j}_\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Reduction to derivative
nodes.statement: We need to show that $\Delta_{\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)\geq0$ for $\eta>0$ small. As before, to do so it suffices to prove the derivative in the origin to be non-negative uniformly in $\varepsilon>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to derivative at origin

nodes.name: Derivative
nodes.statement_short: Compute derivative via gradient of $\bar A$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement:
Since the inequality must hold for any $\varepsilon>0$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$, we have to pick $(\bar a, \bar b)=\arg\min \bar A$. Therefore 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\geq \max(\bar A(\bar a,\bar b), \{A^{\varepsilon,\kappa_1,\kappa_2}(\eta; \bar a,\bar b)\}_{\kappa_1,\kappa_2\in\{-1,1\}})= \min_{ab>\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\bar A( a, b)\quad \forall \varepsilon>0\,,
$$
which combined with (\ref{eq:upperbound.RBM}) proves the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Choose the minimiser; combine with upper bound

nodes.name: Existence of the $RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$ free energy limit
nodes.statement: Let $A_N$ be the free energy of $RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$. Then $\lim_NA_N$ exists $P$-a.s.

nodes.name: A priori bound for $HM_\rho$
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ be the free energy of $HM_{\rho}$. There is $f(\lambda_+,\beta)$ continuous and bounded for which \begin{equation} \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\lambda_+,\beta)\,. \end{equation}
conclusions: There is $f(\lambda_+,\beta)$ continuous and bounded for which \begin{equation} \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\lambda_+,\beta)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: lemma:apriori-bound-HM

nodes.name: Annealed a priori bound ($HM_\rho$)
nodes.statement: \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\lambda_+,\beta)\,.
nodes.label: eq:ann-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement:
Let $a>\lambda_+$ and set for brevity $\lambda^*:=\max_{i\in[N_1]}\lambda_i$. We write $$  rac{1}{N_1+N_2}E[\log Z_{N_1,N_2}]=\sum_{k\geq0}E\left[ rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> kaight ]P((k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka)\,. $$ Inside the conditional expectation we can bound $ H_N(z)\leq a\|z\|^2\, $. Therefore  egin{eqnarray} E\left[ rac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> kaight]&\leq&  rac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log\int\gamma_{N_1,	heta}(dx) \exp\left(\|x\|^2( eta a(k+1))-Nr\left( rac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}ight)ight)
onumber\ &\leq& rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2( eta a(k+1))-N_1r\left( rac{R}{\sqrt N_1}ight)ight)\,
onumber\ &=&\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2( eta a(k+1))-r\left(Right)ight)\,.
onumber \end{eqnarray} On the other hand by assumption  egin{equation} P((k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka)\leq 2e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\,,\quad c>0\,. \end{equation} In conclusion  egin{equation} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq \sum_{k\geq0}e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2( eta a(k+1))-r\left(Right)ight)=:f(a, eta)\,, \end{equation} a continuous bounded function. In particular the estimate holds also for $a	o\lambda_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Condition on the top eigenvalue in slabs, bound each slab by a maximisation over the radius, and sum using the spectral tail bound.

nodes.name: Tail of the top eigenvalue
nodes.statement: P((k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka)\leq 2e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\,,\quad c>0\,.

nodes.name: Summed annealed bound $f(a,\beta)$
nodes.statement: E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq \sum_{k\geq0}e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-r\left(R\right)\right)=:f(a,\beta)\,,

nodes.name: Slab decomposition
nodes.statement:
Let $a>\lambda_+$ and set for brevity $\lambda^*:=\max_{i\in[N_1]}\lambda_i$. We write
$$
\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}E[\log Z_{N_1,N_2}]=\sum_{k\geq0}E\left[\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka\right ]P((k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka)\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Decompose by slabs of the top eigenvalue

nodes.name: Conditional bound
nodes.statement:
Inside the conditional expectation we can bound
$
H_N(z)\leq a\|z\|^2\, 
$. Therefore
\begin{eqnarray}
E\left[\frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka\right]&\leq& \frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log\int\gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx) \exp\left(\|x\|^2(\beta a(k+1))-Nr\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}\right)\right)\nonumber\\
&\leq&\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-N_1r\left(\frac{R}{\sqrt N_1}\right)\right)\,\nonumber\\
&=&\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-r\left(R\right)\right)\,.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Bound each conditional term by a radial maximum

nodes.name: Slab probability
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian tail of slab probabilities

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement_short: Sum into a continuous bounded function

nodes.name: A priori bound for $RBM_{\rho^2}$
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ be the free energy of $RBM_{\rho^2}$. There is $f(\lambda_+,\beta)$ continuous and bounded for which \begin{equation} \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\lambda_+,\beta)\,. \end{equation}
conclusions: There is $f(\lambda_+,\beta)$ continuous and bounded for which \begin{equation} \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\lambda_+,\beta)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: lemma:apriori-bound-HM

nodes.name: Annealed a priori bound ($RBM_{\rho^2}$)
nodes.statement: \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\lambda_+,\beta)\,.
nodes.label: eq:ann-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: Same proof as before, noting \begin{eqnarray} \beta(1-\alpha)\sum_{i}\sigma_ix_iy_i-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt {N_1}}, \frac{\|y\|}{\sqrt {N_2}}\right)&\leq& \beta(1-\alpha)a\|x\|\|y\|-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt {N_1}}\right)\nonumber\\ &\leq&\max_{R_1,R_2}\left(\beta(1-\alpha)aR_1R_2-r(R_1,R_2)\right)\,\nonumber \end{eqnarray} for any $a>\sigma_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Same as previous proof, bounding the bilinear energy by the product of radii.

nodes.name: Tail estimates beyond radius $N^{1/2+\delta}$
nodes.statement: Let $R,\delta>0$, $N\in\mathbb{N}$. It holds for some $C,c>0$ \begin{eqnarray} \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}} \rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}&\leq& C e^{-cN_1^{1+\delta}}\,,\\ \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}} \gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx)\sigma_{R,N_2}(dy)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}&\leq& C e^{-cN_1^{1+\delta}}\,,\\ \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}\cup \{\|y\|^2\geq R^2N_2^{1+\delta}\}} \rho_{N_1,N_2}^2(dxdy)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}&\leq& C e^{-cN_1^{1+\delta}}\,. \end{eqnarray}
conclusions: It holds for some $C,c>0$ \begin{eqnarray} \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}} \rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}&\leq& C e^{-cN_1^{1+\delta}}\,,\\ \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}} \gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx)\sigma_{R,N_2}(dy)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}&\leq& C e^{-cN_1^{1+\delta}}\,,\\ \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}\cup \{\|y\|^2\geq R^2N_2^{1+\delta}\}} \rho_{N_1,N_2}^2(dxdy)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}&\leq& C e^{-cN_1^{1+\delta}}\,. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Configurations with norm beyond $R N^{(1+\delta)/2}$ contribute at most $Ce^{-cN^{1+\delta}}$ to the partition functions.
nodes.label: lemma:coda

nodes.name: Tail estimate for $RBM_{\gamma,\sigma}$
nodes.statement: \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}} \gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx)\sigma_{R,N_2}(dy)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}&\leq& C e^{-cN_1^{1+\delta}}\,,
nodes.label: eq:coda2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: We prove only (\ref{eq:coda1}), as (\ref{eq:coda2}), (\ref{eq:coda3}) are similar. Let us write \begin{eqnarray} \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}} \rho(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}&\leq& e^{-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\delta}}{2\theta}}\int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\delta}\}} \gamma_{N_1,2\theta}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)-N_1r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1}\right)}\nonumber\\ &\leq&e^{-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\delta}}{2\theta}} Z_{N_1,N_2}(2\theta) =\exp\left( (N_1+N_2)A_{N_1,N_2}(2\theta)-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\delta}}{2\theta}\right)\,. \nonumber \end{eqnarray} Here we have emphasised the dependence on $\theta$ of partition function and free energy. Then (\ref{eq:coda1}) follows from Lemma \ref{lemma:apriori-bound-HM}.
nodes.statement_short: Factor out a Gaussian weight on the tail set and bound the rest by the partition function at doubled variance, controlled by the a priori bound.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: We prove only (\ref{eq:coda1}), as (\ref{eq:coda2}), (\ref{eq:coda3}) are similar.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the first estimate

nodes.name: Tail bound
nodes.statement_short: Bound tail by doubled-variance partition function

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Then (\ref{eq:coda1}) follows from Lemma \ref{lemma:apriori-bound-HM}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by the a priori bound

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
Now we are ready to prove the Legendre equivalences of Theorem \ref{th:main}. We shall prove only (\ref{eq:mainHM}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2}); the dual relations (\ref{eq:mainHM-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2-dual}) then follow directly, as one can easily verify the inverse Legendre transformation to be also well defined and involutive. 

We start by $i)$, where we deal with a single Gaussian prior. 
Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta>0$. From now on we will systematically omit the dependence on $\delta$ of the objects we will operate with. Let further $r<N_1^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $R_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\delta}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\delta})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\varepsilon$, and decompose
$
\mathbb{R}^{N_1}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^rS^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\cup T
$, where 
$$

Then we have
\begin{equation} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_1}=\sum_{i=0}^r Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]+\tilde Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}\,,
